text:
maria: Heads-up: rolling BMC + BIOS + NVMe firmware across us-east-2 GPU pool tonight starting 23:00 UTC. Canary = 5 nodes. This build toggles a BIOS secure boot bit by default, but we can decouple. Tagging @kevin @aj @ollie for risk.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: us-east-2 -> canary nodes gpu-us-east2-canary-1..5 | window 23:00-02:00 UTC | changelist CL#3421

kevin: Quick question — last time nvme microcode caused thermal reporting spikes and nodes ended up failing provisioning (disk marked offline). Do we have a rollback plan if GPUs don't provision? :thinking:

aj: Agree with Kevin. Recommend: drain GPUs first, run nvme fw update only during canary, validate SMART and provisioning before any BIOS secure-boot toggle. Also add an explicit `nvme fw-rollback` step in runbook.

ranjit: Reminder: we saw serial console hang after a BMC rewrite in eu-west1 last month — led to OOB flapping for ~30m. For dedicated customers we might want to hold off until we've validated no console regressions. @sre-bot please flag affected projects.

sre-bot: Noted. 2 dedicated projects with reserved capacity in us-east-2 will be notified as "maintenance + potential transient provisioning impact".

maria: We can decouple secure boot toggle. Current payload:
```
bios_update:
  secure_boot: true
  version: 2.13.0
nvme_fw: 4.2.0
bmc_fw: 1.9.4
```
I propose sequence: nvme-only canary -> monitor provisioning & autoscaler headroom -> bios (no secureboot toggle) -> bmc last. If canary ok, schedule secureboot toggles out-of-band.

ollie: If we skip the secure-boot bit we still want nvme fw because it contains a power-management fix that reduces burst temps, but previous 4.1->4.2 lab tests showed NVMe temp reporting differences that triggered kernel offline on older host kernels (2 nodes failed). We should add a pre-check hook for `nvme smart-log` deltas.

kevin: Suggest concrete abort condition: abort if `nvme_offline_count >= 1` OR if provisioning attach failures > 5% over 10m. Also create an ad-hoc metric `nvme_offline_rate` and alert on >0.5% for the rollout window.

maria: Ack. Updating runbook with abort conditions and `nvme smart-log` gating. Runbook: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/oob-fw-roll (internal). I'll kick canary nvme at 23:05 UTC.

[23:12 UTC] system: provsvc observed a provisioning attach failure during canary:
```
[2026-03-17T23:12:07Z] provsvc: attach-gpu gpu-123 failed -> nvme_smart: temp=95C -> nvme-mark-offline
[2026-03-17T23:12:11Z] kernel: nvme0n1: SMART log temp spike, marked inactive
```

aj: I'm watching the canary console. Trying a soft nvme reset on gpu-us-east2-canary-3: `nvme reset --ctrl 0` and re-trigger attach.

maria: Do that. If attach recovers within 5m we continue. If not, invoking `nvme fw-rollback` on affected canary nodes and aborting the full rollout.

kevin: I'll create the metric and a PagerDuty rule. Also bumping autoscaler headroom by +15% for two hours to avoid PLG impact while we observe.

ranjit: Cost FYI: autoscaler headroom increase ~ $6k/hr if fully utilized. Finance and CS will need a note if we expect sustained usage. Flagging @people-ops for notification cadence.

sre-bot: Notification sent to `dedicated-customers` and `platform-ops` lists.

maria: Update: canary status at 23:25 — 3/5 nodes fully updated and passed provisioning smoke. gpu-us-east2-canary-3 had transient attach, recovered after nvme reset and SMART stable. Continuing with nvme canary on remaining two nodes; bios and bmc deferred until nvme fleet looks healthy. I'll post 15m updates here. cc @ops @infra-leads :thumbsup:

kevin: Nice. Once nvme fleet is green we'll schedule a separate maintenance window for BIOS secure-boot toggles (explicit customer opt-in for Dedicated). No surprises.

ollie: Also tracking kernel backports — if the provisioning failures repeat we may need to roll a kernel patch to ignore the transient SMART offline for our host kernel before re-trying rollout.

maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees repeat `nvme-mark-offline` logs, paste them here. We'll hold the BIOS secureboot toggle until after a full fleet validation.
